core_claim: Inconsistency between cognitions, especially between attitudes and freely chosen behaviour, creates discomfort that people reduce by changing attitudes or seeking supporting information.
business_use: Post-purchase reassurance, loyalty programs built on effort, reducing returns

core_claim: When internal cues are weak, people infer their attitudes from their own behaviour and the circumstances in which it occurs.
business_use: Foot-in-the-door sequences in sales, onboarding, and fundraising, avoiding overjustification by rewards

core_claim: People infer the causes of events from covariation information, and the locus, stability, and controllability of those causes shape emotions, blame, and behaviour.
business_use: Service recovery, crisis communication, interpreting reviews and performance explanations

core_claim: People prefer balanced configurations of liking among themselves, another person, and an object, and change one relation to resolve imbalance.
business_use: Celebrity endorsement, sponsorship, and cause-related marketing decisions

core_claim: People learn by observing models, and beliefs in their own capability (self-efficacy) drive choice, effort, persistence, and performance.
business_use: Training design, sales enablement, customer onboarding to self-service

core_claim: Threats to a valued freedom create a motivational state that pushes people to restore the freedom, often by resisting the persuader.
business_use: Scarcity and urgency messaging, personalization, freedom-affirming requests, change management

core_claim: System, information, and service quality shape use and user satisfaction, which produce net benefits that feed back into further use.
business_use: Evaluating enterprise systems, digital services, and IT investments

core_claim: Technology improves performance when its functionality fits the tasks users perform, and use of poorly fitting technology adds little.
business_use: Tool selection, system design, and deployment of AI assistants by task
